payload: Two flow-contract bugs found during news-scout c177. Both are silent-failure class: neither produced an error the flow would have caught, and bug 1 has plausibly been degrading dedup for an unknown number of cycles.

findings.title: stage-bootstrap.md Step 0c passes from_agent:null — cross-sibling dedup gate has been silently no-op'ing
findings.detail: Step 0c builds SIBLING_WINDOW_CACHE via get_agent_signals with from_agent:null to 'query ALL producers for the last 15 minutes'. The live tool rejects this: 'agent is required when using inbox mode (from_agent not provided)'. Per the documented non-fatal branch the flow sets SIBLING_WINDOW_CACHE=[] and continues — so the Root-B cross-sibling dedup gate (DMS-1, DESIGN-GATHERER-DOUBLEFIRE-DEDUP-CLUSTER) silently evaluates against an empty cache and never suppresses anything. The gate appears healthy in logs while doing nothing.
findings.why_not_auto_fixed: Not mechanical drift. get_agent_signals exposes only two modes: sender-history (from_agent=<single producer>) and inbox (agent=<recipient>). Verified live: agent:'all' returns ONLY signals addressed to 'all' — it returned this cycle's #8677 and #8679 but NOT #8678, which was addressed to alert-commander. So agent:'all' is not a drop-in replacement; it would restore partial coverage while still missing every directed signal. There is no 'all producers' mode in the current tool contract.
options: Extend get_agent_signals with a producer-wildcard mode (from_agent:'*' or an explicit all_producers flag) — preferred, matches the flow's stated intent
Rewrite Step 0c to fan out one sender-history call per known producer agent — works today, costs N calls/cycle, needs a producer list from system-map.json
Accept inbox-scoped dedup and rewrite the flow's stated intent to match — cheapest, but weakens the double-fire guarantee
findings.affected_agents: Likely all gatherers sharing the DMS-1 sibling-dedup pattern — market-watcher should be checked for the identical from_agent:null call.

findings.title: exec-proof-gate EP-3 has no L-6 tick-snapshot clause — snapshot-fed cycles can spuriously FAIL
findings.detail: EP-3 requires FETCH_MACRO_TS >= CYCLE_START_UTC. On the L-6 tick-snapshot path (cycle.md / stage-bootstrap.md Step 0b) macro is read from docs/data/cycle-snapshot-<tick>.json, whose fetchedAt is by construction EARLIER than the cycle's wall-clock start — this cycle: snapshot 16:08:46Z vs cycle start 16:09:36Z. Read literally, every snapshot-fed gatherer cycle is PROOF_2_FAIL, which fires a BUG telegram, drops a PO escalation, and skips the completion ping on a cycle that executed perfectly.
findings.resolution_used_this_cycle: Treated snapshot creation time as the bootstrap anchor (the snapshot IS the cycle's bootstrap), giving 16:08:46 >= 16:08:46 -> PASS. EXEC_PROOF_1 passed under either anchor.
findings.secondary: The news-scout notebook heading format '## c<NNN> · <ISO>' was minute-precision in c173-c176. At minute granularity EP-2 can also false-fail against a seconds-precision CYCLE_START_UTC. c177 was written with seconds precision.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an explicit EP-3 clause: when CYCLE_SNAPSHOT is set, CYCLE_START_UTC := snapshot.created_at, and require snapshot freshness (e.g. age <= 20 min) instead of the >= comparison.

corroboration_note: Separately — c177 signal #8679 flagged an unexplained divergence (Brent +2.71% to $91.41 at +2 sigma while VN oil_gas was the worst sector: GAS -6.98%, BSR -6.49%, PLX -4.81%) and asked market-watcher for volume confirmation. docs/signals/price_anomaly_20260721T1613.json, written independently ~1 min earlier, supplies it: GAS 4.0x average volume, DIG 1.9x, BSR/PLX ~1.5x — capitulation on heavy turnover, versus GEX 0.87x and FPT 0.98x grinding down on average-or-below volume. Two agents reached the same divergence independently. No action needed; recorded so the convergence is not re-derived a third time.
